checks.explanation: D-selection is on page 1 and itemized prices begin on page 1, so the disclosure is on the same page as the prices it accompanies.
The list uses the built-in basic-services fee option with no separate basic services line item, so there is no basic-services includesText to evaluate.
No second mandatory fee for services, facilities or overhead appears; the only basic-services fee described is the $2,195 fee in the casket-price notice.
D-embalming is on page 1 and the Embalming $795 price is on page 1, so it is on the same page as the price.
No text states embalming is required for direct cremation, immediate burial, or closed-casket service; the embalming disclosure states embalming is usually not required.
D-alt-container is on page 2 and the direct cremation $1,595 to $1,945 range is on page 2, so it is on the same page.
Direct cremation is offered with purchaser-provided container, fiberboard container, and wood box options, with no statement that a casket is required.
The direct cremation includesText lists removal, transportation and authorizations, but no cash-advance list is shown billing a separate crematory fee.
Forwarding, receiving, direct cremation and immediate burial each have itemized prices, and no goods or services are shown offered only inside a package or description.
The list contains required single-price items for forwarding, receiving, direct cremation and immediate burial but no optional combination package sold at one price.
No text asserts that law, a cemetery or a crematory requires a purchase; the only law-related statements are the prescribed not-required disclosures.
No text claims goods or services delay decomposition long-term or protect the body from gravesite substances.
No other wording undercuts a required disclosure, and the required disclosures use the prescribed wording.
